Seasonal Wildlife · the full-pool design · simulated 9 Oct · built and run on the rig 12 Oct 2026

Cast Pipeline Trace

Your design of 9 Oct (evening), simulated on DF's own raws for six embarks. The pool is no longer the short list DF stocked on the region: every creature in the raws is a candidate, filtered first by wild and natural, then BIOME, SAVAGE, GOOD/EVIL and the world's real-world-extinct rule, then split into seven layers (land-ground, land-flying, ocean, freshwater, cavern 1, 2, 3) and four seasons. Each of those lists feeds one season cast with the slot table you set for its layer. The design is now built into the engine (v7.5) and has run on the rig: the results come first, in On the rig. The sections after it are the desk simulation the build followed. Every table sorts by a click on its header; categorical columns filter.

What changes, in numbers

Land-ground pools grow several-fold

6 → 22 species on the lake fort, 3 → 27 on the ocean fort: what DF stocked against everything the biome allows.

Every species DF stocked is still in

On all three real forts the new pool contains every species in DF's population list, except the locked unliving cave species, the lava-only magma crab, demons, and one damselfly. The biome reading matches DF's own stocking.

Variety across the year

21 different species cast on the lake fort's land-ground over four seasons, 26 in the ocean fort's sea. The x0.01-per-earlier-cast weight spreads the picks.

Caverns get stranger with depth

Mean weirdness of the casts: cavern 1 0.24, cavern 2 0.47, cavern 3 0.72 (0 = a real animal's cave form, 1 = wholly alien).

On the rig: a full year on v7.5 (12 Oct)

The design on this page is the engine (seasonal-wildlife v7.5, branch v7.5-fullpool). It ran on the three region19 forts for a whole year, from early spring through winter and 17 days into the next year, one replicate each, with DF restarted for every fort: run X4v75b, on the code after the review fixes. Earlier runs (X3v75 to X3v75c, spring to autumn) found and fixed four bugs (below). The rules applied on 13 Oct (below) came after this run and have not run on the rig yet.

The year turn changes nothing

3 / 3 forts ended with the casts they began with, none rebuilt at the new year, and every arrival of the new year (122 in all) was cast for its season.

Two pass, one fault found and fixed

2 / 3 pass every check. The lake fort's one fault: a cavern group sent off at the autumn change was released again 1.1 days later at a depth its species is not cast at. The release step now skips sent-off groups.

Species DF never stocked arrive

268 arrivals came from population entries the tool created, 97 of them in the caverns. 3,020 managed arrivals in all.

What the runs found

runresultcause and fix
X3v75stopped after the lake fortEach cavern's mask was lost at every load (the saved casts dropped their version on reload), so every depth stayed open: 10 animals came in through a cavern their species was not cast in. Fixed; and a species DF stocked in one cavern but cast in another now gets an entry at the cast depth.
X3v75bocean pass; lake one fault; brook hung four timesThe tool could freeze DF. DF picks a cavern wave by raw FREQUENCY among one region tile's stocked animals in one cave; when every one reads 0 the pick never ends and the simulation stops while the screen still draws. A guard now keeps one species of each such group at 1.
A pike in autumn, cast for spring and winter: created entries for freshwater species were filed where no season reached them; each now follows the cast it was made for.
No sponges on the ocean fort: the sponge pass looked only for water-feature entries, which sea life does not have. Fixed.
X3v75call three pass, no hangsSpring to early autumn on the final code of the build.
X4v75bfull year: ocean and brook pass; lake one faultA sent-off group released again. A DF wave the cavern gate holds back is released later, oldest first; one sent off by the season change could still be picked, so a draltha, cast only in cavern 1 for autumn, was released in cavern 2 1.1 days in (two more on the ocean fort, inside the day). The release now skips sent-off groups, as it skipped trimmed ones. The analyser also scored two albatross groups "not left in 10 days": albatrosses are cast on the water layer in summer and gated as land, so the cast's own birds stayed on the map; the tool's leave check found none of the sent-off ones still there. Scored now as in the cast.

Crowdedness and diversity through the year

Every wild animal on the map in run X4v75b, one bar per day of the year: the height is how crowded the layer was, each segment one species (so the number of segments is its diversity that day), coloured by animal type. Sponges (placed scenery, never cast) are not counted, and a fully aquatic species recorded on land is counted in the water chart (amphibians stay on land). Each chart has its own fort selector. Dashed lines mark the season changes, when the casts turn over. Each chart's y-axis fits its own data, so read the axis when comparing forts. Hover a day for its species; each chart's table lists them all.

Applied 13 Oct: your apex decisions

Your answers to the apex review, now in the simulation (every table on this page is regenerated with them) and ported to the engine. Not yet run on the rig.

  • The audit bug is fixed. The audit read every row's apex tiers after its last embark, so one embark's wiring stood for all: the grimeling showed as an evil freshwater apex everywhere and the harpy nowhere. Tiers are now read with each row; the harpy and the nightwing are in the evil flying rows.
  • Two new freshwater apexes: the tigerfish (tropical lakes and rivers) and the anaconda (into tropical lakes and rivers through the table below).
  • The dingo is narrowed to arid, open and dry country; the temperate wetlands it held alone get the black bear, the wolf, the cougar and the jaguar.
  • The apex draw's pack bonus is x1.5 (it was the cast-wide x3; the pack is also counted in group size). Every other slot keeps x3.
  • Tool-side biome additions for the apexes DF keeps in tropical subtypes, and a wider evil roster on evil regions (table). The savage, alignment and extinct gates still apply per biome, and the engine creates population entries for cast species DF has not stocked, so DF sends them itself.
  • Giant bug apexes: the giant mantis and four more giant bugs the raws leave without CARNIVORE are read as predators; they and the three giant arachnids are true apexes in any savage or evil land biome, a calm evil one included, and the fliers can take the land-ground apex as well as land-flying.

What the six embarks show

  • The diversity is there. The lake fort's land-ground pool is 22 species where DF stocked 6; the savage forest's is 233 (its extinct species, giants and animal people all qualify). The casts stay the size you set; the variety shows across the year.
  • A marsh has few walkers. The brook fort's land-ground pool is 8 species: most marsh animals are amphibious and now belong to the water layer, as you ruled. Its freshwater pool is 21.
  • The apex rotates. Under the rebuilt rule the apex differs between seasons on 34 of the 34 layers with an apex slot. The ocean fort's sea goes sperm whale → shark mako longfin → shark hammerhead → sperm whale; the arctic coast's land bear polar → bear grizzly → bear polar → wolf. Where it stays put, only one predator is eligible: the dingo is the only flagged hunter of a temperate savanna or marsh in DF's raws (lake and brook forts).
  • Murky pools work as a mini roster once the pool's fish slot can draw DF's pool fish and amphibians, which are all vermin: on the evil savanna the year casts FISH_LUNGFISH, LEECH, POND_TURTLE, RIVER OTTER, TOAD.
  • River-only freshwater has no apex, as you listed; the alligator and similar predators take its one meso slot.
  • Extinct species follow the world setting. With "any wild region" the arctic coast gains 14 extinct species (woolly mammoth and woolly rhinoceros among them); with "savage regions only" the calm real forts get none and the savage forest gets all that fit.
  • Odd fits come from DF's own raws, not the filter: an alligator on a cold river (its raws allow any temperate river), a capybara on a temperate saltwater marsh, penguins on an arctic coast.
  • Caverns are the same three pools on every fort (DF's cave species are not biome-bound), so only the draw differs between forts.

Two odds: being cast, and arriving

The tool weighs a species twice, at two different times, by two different mechanisms.

stagewhenwho decideswhat sets the odds
1. Inclusion: is the species in a season's cast?once, at embark (or first enable, or a redraw); all 28 casts at once, in a random orderthe tool (castYear, castGrow)the seed's high-value test, food-web links into the emptiest slot, and the pick weights: x3 pack hunters, x0.2 giants, x0.1 animal people, x0.01 per cast already built that holds the species; the apex draw (size, the same weights)
2. Appearance: which cast species comes in the next wave?every wave, all season, every yearDF, drawing from the region's population entriesDF picks in proportion to each creature's raw FREQUENCY. The tool rewrites FREQUENCY to the cast's ladder (the pyramid: grazers and prey common, predators rarer, apexes at most 5; castLadder writes one number per species, CAVERN.apply copies it into the raw) and holds every out-of-season species' entry at zero, so only cast species can be drawn. Apexes are placed by the tool's scheduler.

Where the x0.01 belongs: at inclusion. That is where it is now, and where it does what you want: across the year it makes a species unlikely to be cast in a second season while others are free, so the four casts of a layer differ, and a species that is cast twice is cast because nothing else fits (a thin pool, or the only apex). Applied to appearance instead (a grizzly cast all year arriving at x1, x0.01, x0.01², x0.01³), three things break:

  • Hollow casts. The grizzly keeps its summer, autumn and winter slots but almost never arrives in them, so those casts show one apex short and the food web the cast was built on does not appear on the map.
  • DF cannot hold the numbers. FREQUENCY is a whole number per creature, 1 to 100 in practice; 50 x 0.01 = 0.5 and 50 x 0.0001 both round to 0 or the floor of 1. Only one step of the decay is representable.
  • It needs seasonal FREQUENCY. Today's ladder writes one number per species for the year; a decaying odds would have to be rewritten at every season change (the season timer can, at the cost of one more write pass).

So x0.01 stays at inclusion (confirmed 12 Oct): each cast built before this one that holds the species multiplies its weight by 0.01. Arrival odds are then the ladder's, the same every year, so nothing needs a yearly reset. Population entries are never reset: each wave debits its entry, and a species whose entry runs out is gone from the fort's region (local extinction).

How the region's population list is made to match the casts

The tool does not overwrite DF's entries; it masks them. DF draws a wave only from entries with animals left, so for each managed species the tool sets the entry's count to zero (and marks it extinct) whenever the species is out of season or not cast, parking that count in its reserve, and puts the same count back when the species' cast season comes (applyLive, holdOutOfSeason). DF's own stocking is untouched underneath and comes back whole when the tool is turned off. A cast species DF never stocked gets a new entry beside DF's (phase 5), masked the same way and removed at off. The reserve only ever holds an entry's own animals; it creates none.

In the caverns the mask works per cavern: each has its own cast, so a species cast in cavern 1 alone keeps its cavern 2 and 3 entries at zero, and a species DF stocked in one cavern but cast in another gets an entry where it is cast. One limit comes from DF itself (found on the rig, 12 Oct): when every stocked animal of one region tile in one cave has FREQUENCY 0, DF's wave pick never ends and the game stops. The tool's cap gate can do exactly that, so after every FREQUENCY write a guard puts one species of each such group back at 1.

Build order

Because the repeat weight counts casts already built, the cast built first gets the unpenalised pick of every species eligible all year. Built Spring first, the high-weight species (pack hunters x3, high-value seeds) gathered in Spring; built in a random order (seeded by site and year), each season gets its fair share. Measured over 40 simulated years on each of the six embarks, counting every non-apex cast place of a species eligible on its layer in all four seasons:

build orderpack hunters Springpack hunters Summerpack hunters Autumnpack hunters Winterpack placesall Springall Summerall Autumnall Winterconcentration
Spring first30.5%25.4%21.5%22.6%5,18224.7%24.8%24.8%25.7%38.5%
random order23.4%26.2%23.8%26.6%5,14724.6%24.9%24.7%25.8%36.4%

The rule this produces (confirmed 12 Oct): a species goes, at random, into whichever season × layer casts it is eligible for, and every further appearance is penalised x0.01 cumulatively, in whatever order the casts happen to be built. It is discouraged from a second season and from a second layer in the same season alike.

The total per season is the same either way, because each cast has fixed slot counts; what the order changes is which species fill them. "Concentration" is the mean share of a species' casts that fall in its most common season (25% would be perfectly even).

Who can hold the apex

Rebuilt 10 Oct. A species can be drawn for the apex slot of a layer when it is:

  • a LARGE_PREDATOR species (land, flying and caverns; caverns keep their sentients in the sentient slot);
  • a giant of any predator, mesopredators included (giant fox, giant badger, giant kestrel);
  • an animal person whose root animal is eligible (bear man, cougar man, quetzalcoatlus man), drawn at x0.1 as all animal people;
  • on water layers, one of the engine's curated water apexes (orca, sperm whale, great white, crocodiles, the large sharks) or a giant or animal person of one; DF's other LARGE_PREDATOR water species (sea lamprey, frill shark, blacktip) take meso, as before;
  • a raptor of 2,000 cm³ or more on land-flying (eagle, the large owls, osprey; never a scavenger);
  • a real-life apex that DF does not tag, below;
  • a species the biomes × region audit promotes or wires in for a biome that had too few apexes (approved 12 Oct, applied);
  • on an evil region, the harpy on land-flying (an EVIL LARGE_PREDATOR raptor, kept out before only by its sentience) and the grimeling on freshwater (the only EVIL water hunter besides the sea monster; DF tags it NO_EAT and NO_DRINK, so it is let through as a hand-wired apex). A lake is the only freshwater layer with an apex slot; on a river or murky pools the grimeling can take meso (it is too large for the murky-pool roster).

The draw then weights each by the square root of its group size against the largest (a pack's mean size times the adult size), x3 for pack hunters, x0.01 for each cast it is already on this year (counted only once drawn: the year's 28 casts are built together at its start), x0.2 giants and x0.1 animal people. That is what puts the orca beside the sperm whale: a pod of six orcas outweighs one whale.

Real-life apexes DF does not tag LARGE_PREDATOR

Every carnivore in the raws without the flag (56) and the large predators DF does not even mark CARNIVORE were checked against their real ecology. "Apex" joins the draw; "local" holds the apex only where no true apex is in season (the top of a small or depleted community). Several are not CARNIVORE in DF's raws; the CARNIVORE fix below now reads them as predators.

The CARNIVORE fix

Real-life hunters DF does not tag CARNIVORE (or BONECARN), which the tool used to read as prey (12 Oct: applied). Upper-level predators only: mid-level fish (cod, carp, bluefish, skate) stay in the fish slot and penguins stay shore birds. A fish-eating bird gains the predator role but is not a raptor, so it never holds the flying apex. In the engine this is a set of 'predator' entries in MODEL.ROLE.

Biomes × region × apex audit

Built programmatically over the whole creature list (scripts/castsim/apex_audit.py): every surface biome (27 land, 3 oceans, temperate and tropical lakes) under six region types (not savage or savage, × good, neutral or evil; extinct species under UNTAMED_WILDS, so only on savage regions), through the same filters and layer split as the casts. For each it counts the layer's potential cast members and, per season, the species that can hold the apex. A row is short when some season has fewer than two true apexes. Rivers and murky pools have no apex slot; caverns do not depend on the region.

Candidates for the short rows

Generated, not hand-picked. Promote: every resident predator that cannot hold the apex today, the resident local apexes (lynx, coyote, wolverine) first, then by group size against the largest resident. Wire: every species that is a true apex of the same layer in another biome of the same region type and climate band, scored by fauna overlap (the share of this biome's residents that also live in the candidate's biomes). The automatic proposal takes local promotions, then wires with overlap 0.5 or more, then other promotions, then other wires, until every season has two true apexes. The scores say how well a candidate fits DF's own fauna, not real-life range: a wired dingo in the taiga scores well because DF's dingo shares most of the taiga's animals. Approved 12 Oct and applied to the casts on this page (the automatic proposal of each short row).

Judgement calls in this simulation

Everything the design left open and the simulation had to decide. Each is a single rule you can change.

decisionwhat the simulation does
land-ground slotsnot specified: kept the v7.4 land cast without its raptor, bird and sentient slots (apex 1, meso 2, grazer 2, ground prey 2, vermin 3).
ranges"1-2" and "2-3": each cast draws its count inside the range, so cast sizes vary from season to season.
apex rulerebuilt 10 Oct: the apex is a weighted draw among the eligible predators in season, not the largest. Eligible: LARGE_PREDATOR species, giants of any predator, animal people whose root is eligible, the curated water apexes, raptors of 2,000 cm3 and up, and the real-life apexes DF does not flag (table on the page). Weight: the square root of group size (adult size x the pack's mean size) against the largest, x1.5 for pack hunters (13 Oct; x3 before: the pack was counted twice, in group size and again as the bonus), x0.01 per cast the species is already on this year, x0.2 giants, x0.1 animal people. No size floor (a 10% floor cut lions and hyenas beside a pair of ogres, and the great white beside an orca pod). The rest can still take meso. Water layers: only the curated water apexes (and their giants and animal people) are eligible, as in the engine; DF's other LARGE_PREDATOR water species (sea lamprey, frill shark, blacktip) take meso.
hand-wiringthe audit's automatic proposal is approved and applied (12 Oct): per biome and region type, promoted residents and wired apexes are true apexes; a wired species is treated as living in the biome. Evil regions also get the harpy on land-flying and the grimeling on freshwater (the grimeling let through the natural filter as a hand-wired apex).
local apexesa "local" real-life apex (lynx, coyote, wolverine, gar, grouper...) holds the apex only when no true apex is in season; with none of either, the largest non-sentient predator is promoted (the old fallback, still your open question).
spongesthe sponge and the giant sponge are placed like plants on the bed (30 Sep, 12 Oct): they pass the filters, enter the water layers they live in, and take no cast slot; the sponge man passes as a natural filter-feeder creature and can be cast.
CARNIVORE fixreal-life hunters DF does not tag CARNIVORE are read as predators (table on the page): upper-level fish and small sharks, seals, walrus, mink, weasel, fish-eating seabirds and the white stork. Mid-level fish (cod, carp, bluefish, skate) and penguins are left as they were.
reusex0.01^N at cast inclusion, N = the number of casts already built that hold the species (any layer, any season). The 28 casts are built at once at embark (or first enable, or a redraw) in a random order, seeded by site and year, so no season gets the first pick of the species eligible all year (a Spring-first order gave Spring the unpenalised pick; measured on the page).
biome additionstool-side (13 Oct): apex predators DF keeps in tropical subtypes, which worldgen rarely makes, also live in the realistic ecotypes beside them (lion, tiger, hyena, cheetah, python, monitor lizard, cougar; leopard to mountains, jaguar, black bear and wolf to temperate wetlands; table on the page). The dingo is kept to arid, open and dry country. On evil regions the evil roster is widened (beak dog to every wetland, strangler and blendec foul to forests, ogre to mountains and deserts) and the nightwing is the evil desert flier. The gates still apply per biome.
giant bug apexesgiant bugs eat what they can catch (13 Oct): the mantis, dragonfly, tick, mosquito and roach are read as predators, and they and the three giant arachnids are true apexes in any savage or evil land biome, a calm evil one included; the fliers can take the land-ground apex as well as land-flying. The x0.2 giant weight still applies.
new water apexesthe tigerfish (tropical lakes and rivers) and the anaconda (wired into tropical lakes and rivers) are freshwater apexes (13 Oct).
river-only apexno apex slot (your list has none); flagged predators there can take the meso slot.
fill fallbacka slot with room and no candidate linked to the cast is filled anyway from its eligible species ("no link"), so no slot stays empty while candidates exist; the food web is computed after the draw on every layer, as you asked for land-flying.
amphibiansan amphibious (water-breathing, not aquatic) creature never enters land-ground; if its BIOME names a fort land biome it can enter the freshwater layer (its shore slot), and on a saltwater marsh, swamp or mangrove the ocean layer.
shore and fliersa shore creature or a waterbird eats an aquatic creature no larger than itself (or 20,000 cm3), and aquatic vermin.
murky pools"small" = adult size up to 20,000 cm3 for the pool mini roster; DF's pool fish and amphibians are vermin (lungfish, pond turtle, toad), so the pool's fish slot draws fish-class and amphibious vermin too (a species drawn as fish is not also drawn as vermin).
cavern sentientsa sentient cavern species (troll, blind cave ogre, gorlak, animal people, troglodyte) fills only the sentient slot.
weirdnessa first-cut 0-1 score per cavern species (table in the step-through); cavern 1 picks weight (1-w)^2, cavern 2 the middle, cavern 3 w^2. DF's own raw depth range still decides which caverns a species can live in.
region biomesa real fort's biomes are the 3x3 world tiles around it (DF draws a block's wildlife from all nine region neighbours); each biome takes the savagery and evil of the nearest tile that has it.
alignmentGOOD species only where the biome is good (evil 0-32), EVIL only where evil (66+); cavern species are exempt (v7: alignment only limits taming).
cavern savagerycaverns ignore surface savagery: DF stocks savage cave species (giant cave spider) on calm forts.
extinct ruleDF's raws tag every real-world-extinct species SAVAGE; the world's REAL_WORLD_EXTINCT setting is read in place of that tag (UNTAMED_WILDS: savage regions only; ISOLATED: small world regions of 5 tiles or less, savage or not, as DF stocks them on region16; WILDERNESS and DOMESTICATED: any wild region). Extinct animal people stay savage-only, as all animal people.
extinct settingregion19's REAL_WORLD_EXTINCT cannot be read without DF (world.raws.param_real_world_extinct); the real forts assume UNTAMED_WILDS, the install's default preset value.
wilda creature is wild when it has a BIOME and either LARGE_ROAMING or a vermin tag, colony insects (VERMIN_SOIL_COLONY: ants, bees, termites) included (DF's own test for region populations).

Building it into seasonal-wildlife

Built 12 Oct, every phase below, and run on the rig (results). The table is the plan as it stood before the build, with its line numbers in v7.4; phase 5's freshwater entries were solved without a water-feature creator, as surface entries filed under the species' water key, which DF draws waves from. The original text follows.

A pass through the engine (scripts/seasonal-wildlife.lua on v7.4-onebuilder 834f92e, 19,102 lines; line numbers below) for the shortest path from today's code to the patterns on this page. Most of the machinery exists: the engine already scans every raw creature against the embark's biomes, already creates population entries on land and in caverns, and already places units with an on-site population reference. Order matters: each phase can ship and be checked on the rig before the next.

Decided (12 Oct)

  • Casts are built once, at embark, at first enable, or when the player asks for a redraw; all 28 at once, in a random order seeded by site and year. They are not redrawn at a new year.
  • The x0.01 repeat weight is an inclusion weight (section above): x0.01 per cast already built that holds the species. Arrival odds are the ladder's, the same each year; population entries run down naturally, and a species whose entry is spent is locally extinct. The reserve is unchanged.
  • Created entries are removed when the tool is turned off. The tool records every entry it creates (region tile, race, master and live row) in its saved config; off zeroes them, lets or sends their units off the map, clears any unit's population reference to them, and then deletes both rows, next to the reserve give-back (RESERVE.giveBack 3071). A unit still pointing at a deleted entry is the risk to test first. Phase 5.
  • The audit's proposals are approved, with the harpy and grimeling for evil regions: a wiring table the engine reads beside MODEL.ROLE.

Settled by the build

  • Freshwater entries. No water-feature creator was needed: a surface entry for the species, masked by its freshwater cast, is enough for DF to send it (the longnose gar, pike and sturgeon arrived this way).
  • Wired species on the map remain untested: the three rig forts wire none (see Not yet seen on the rig).

Method notes

Raws. DF 53.16's vanilla and extinct creature files compiled as DF compiles them (COPY_TAGS_FROM, the GIANT and ANIMAL_PERSON variations, castes, derived flags, aggregate biome tokens expanded), as in the earlier trace. Classification (guild, habitat, size, pet value, the 83 extinct corrections) is the engine's classify, mirrored in scripts/castsim/engine.py. The design is scripts/castsim/design.py; the runner is design_run.py. Random draws are seeded per embark, layer and season, so one run is one possible year.
